pr.title: Create a fresh Cipher for each key operation
pr.body:
## What this changes

In `SecretKeyWrapper`, the app wraps a secret key with the public key and unwraps a blob as an AES secret key with the private key. RVSec reported that `SecretKeyWrapper.unwrap` reinitializes the Java `Cipher` after wrapping on the missing-key-file path; its rule does not permit that order.

I changed `wrap` and `unwrap` to create a fresh `Cipher` for each operation instead of sharing one. The transformation, keys, modes, and wrapped-key representation remain unchanged.

I found this while running the app under RVSec, a runtime checker for how apps use the Java crypto and TLS APIs.

The project builds with this change (`assembleDebug`).

I'm a Computer Engineering student at the University of Brasília (UnB), working on a research project on Android app analysis. Happy to adjust this to the project's conventions.

## How it was checked

- [ ] Ran the app and exercised the change
- [ ] Checked the light, dark and black themes if the change is visual
- [ ] Added or updated a test where the change is testable

## Commit subject prefix

The changelog is generated from commit subjects. Use a prefix so the entry lands in the right
section, or leave it off and it will be filed under Improvement:

`feat:` new  ·  `fix:` fix  ·  `perf:` / `refactor:` / `build:` improvement  ·  `docs:` / `chore:`
/ `test:` / `ci:` left out  ·  add `!` before the colon for a breaking change.

Thank you for finding this and for the clear write-up, @jpantonow. The fix is merged.

Our master branch only accepts signed commits, so I rebased your commit onto master and signed it on our side. You're still the author of the commit that landed (e5e8981). Good luck with the RVSec research!
